description: ODC (shared-contracts pilot, phase 2): REFACTOR records and the static entity itself that this job did not create - repoint, delete, duplicate. The base is job:static-entity-lifecycle, so WfClaimPhase already has the records Intake, Assessment, Closed and WfEscalated, and the inherited default of WfClaimFile.StageId says Entities.WfClaimPhase.WfEscalated (the only real consumer of a record). Three things that only a refactoring job measures: (A) `replace` between two records of the same entity rewrites the expression of the consumer (Entities.WfClaimPhase.WfEscalated -> Entities.WfClaimPhase.Closed) and leaves the source record with no consumers - it is the step that makes the following delete possible WITHOUT force; (B) `delete` of a record with no consumers is accepted, and the record disappears from the entity (Records 4 -> 3); (C) `duplicate` of the whole static entity copies the entity with attributes AND records (name with the platform's suffix), and the copy is born with no consumers. The `move` of a record does not enter here: the reading order of records is the value of Order (OrderByAttribute), not the position in the tree - see the refusal measured in tests/jobs-odc-negative/move-static-record.json. Everything is read before and after with get/usages/dump: the counter of the verb delivers nothing by itself.

ops._why: (0) BEFORE: the inherited default says Entities.WfClaimPhase.WfEscalated - written by the base job (13a). It is the expression that the replace (2) has to rewrite without this job touching it.
(1a) BEFORE: real 1 - the default of WfClaimFile.StageId. Compare with the usages (3a), which has to give real 0.
(1b) BEFORE: real 0 - the target record is not yet cited by anyone. Compare with the usages (3b).

(2) CHANGE 1 - REPOINT: all external consumers of the record WfEscalated now cite Closed. Both sides are IStaticEntityRecord, so there is no force. The kernel checks in the model itself that 0 consumers were left at the source and that all of them were found at the target; if not, the op fails. The text of the expression is rewritten by the platform (ReplaceReferences), not by this job.
(2b) AFTER: the DefaultValue says Entities.WfClaimPhase.Closed. Nobody wrote this text - compare with the get (0).
(3a) real 0: the source record was left orphaned. It is this that makes the delete (4) pass without force.
(3b) real 1: the consumer that was on WfEscalated is now here, with the same key.

(4) CHANGE 2 - DELETE a record WITHOUT consumers: accepted without force (the IRecordAttributeValue of the record itself are children, not consumers). The refusal of the same delete WITH the consumer still linked is measured in tests/jobs-odc-negative/delete-static-record-in-use.json.
(4b) AFTER: Records 3 (it was 4 after the base). Attributes is still 4: deleting a record does not touch the schema.

ops.name: WfEscalated
ops._why: (4c) empty list: the record disappeared from the module.

(5) CHANGE 3 - DUPLICATE the whole static entity. The name of the copy is whatever the platform chooses (suffix), the copy enters at the end of the ESpace and is born WITHOUT consumers. Read the get (5b) and the dump (5c) to know what was copied: attributes, records and the values per record.
(5b) the copy: EntityKind Static, Attributes 4, Records 3, Identifier/Label/OrderBy pointing to the COPIED attributes (new keys), Name with the platform's suffix.

(5c) the tree of the copy: 4 IEntityAttribute, 3 IStaticEntityRecord with the same Identifier (Intake, Assessment, Closed) and one IRecordAttributeValue per attribute with the same texts - all keys new.
(5d) real 0 except for the IAttribute of the anonymous record that the platform generates for the copy: nobody outside cites the duplicated entity.
(5e) the original keeps its consumers (the default and the IAttribute of its anonymous record): duplicating does not move consumers.

(6) CLEANUP with declared force: the copy has no author consumers, but in ODC every entity brings an IAnonymousStructure '<Name> Record' that cites it (the IAttribute of that anonymous record), and that platform-generated consumer is not derived for the kernel - the same reason delete-entity-whole.json needs force. Here the force only breaks that generated consumer; no author consumer exists (usages 5d).

ops.name: WfClaimPhase
ops._why: (7) END: only the original (and its anonymous record) answer to this name; the copy and its anonymous record disappeared.
(8) the final tree of the original: 4 attributes and 3 records (Intake, Assessment, Closed), the inherited consumer pointing to Closed.
